newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher amid rebound in oil prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher amid rebound in oil prices.

text.p: NYMEX crude rebounded Tuesday as a threats by petroleum industry workers in Nigeria to go on strike helped drive short covering throughout the oil complex after Monday's sharp decline, traders said.

"The Nigerian news definitely got the ball rolling today, but once we got above $21.00 (in crude) there was a good amount of short covering," said Bob Yawger, trader with E.D. & F. Man International in New York.
April crude settled up 29 cents at $21.00 a barrel, after rising as high as $21.31.
March heat ended up 1.35 cents a gallon at 56.82 cents. March gasoline ended up 1.99 cents at 62.23 cents a gallon.

Increasing crude supply and mild temperatures have pressured oil prices over the past month. Prompt crude and heating oil have fallen about 20 percent since late January. Dealers said heat's rise Tuesday was due almost entirely to short covering, but they said gasoline attracted fund buying.

After losing 4.26 cents a gallon from Thursday's open to Monday's close, traders noted gasoline represented a buying opportunity ahead of the traditional spring gasoline rally. The rally anticipates the summer driving season.

Meanwhile, workers of Nigeria's Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR), which processes export documents for oil shipments, have threatened to go on strike from Friday if the backlog of their salaries are not paid, oil ministry sources said on Tuesday.
Dealers downplayed the significance of the possible strike on the market, saying the workers were not responsible for production, so there was no imminent threat to supply.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) was expected to report weekly oil inventory data Tuesday evening, and traders wanted to square positions in case the data held surprises.
Traders expect crude stocks to grow between one and three million barrels for the week ended February 21 as refiners cut crude usage to continue their winter maintenance.
This would be the fifth consecutive time the API has reported a build in crude stocks.
A bullish draw in oil stocks could send oil prices higher, but dealers said the downtrend in oil prices remains in place.
"I think we may test $20.50, and we may enter a $20.50 to $21.50 range for now," said a New York dealer of crude.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
